extracted.intended_audience: technical writers, product makers, and developers planning to submit posts to Hacker News
extracted.subtask_description: Advice and practical criteria for when and how to submit link posts, Show HN, or Ask HN to Hacker News to maximize engagement while following site norms. Covers timing windows, submission type, etiquette, and pre/post-submit checklist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing — default US-morning window
rubrics_metrics.description: For a normal technical post, start with Tuesday through Thursday, roughly 14:00 to 17:00 UTC (7am–10am Pacific, 10am–1pm Eastern).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This lines up with when the US technical audience is awake and active and with practical launch advice in other HN guides. Use this as a reasonable default for maximum raw audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing — experimental low-competition window
rubrics_metrics.description: If your goal is lower competition (best chance per post rather than biggest total audience), consider Sunday night Pacific, especially around midnight to 1am Pacific.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyses of ~23,000 posts argue fewer submissions then give strong posts an early push. Useful for niche, weird, or narrowly targeted posts; treat this as an experimental alternative rather than universal truth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing — weekends and niche posts
rubrics_metrics.description: Weekends are viable for side projects, longer reads, and curiosity-driven posts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different goals (maximum audience vs. lower competition) require different timing tradeoffs; weekends can work when the content matches weekend reader behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand HN ranking complexity
rubrics_metrics.description: HN ranking is not just votes plus time; it includes flags, anti-abuse software, overheating penalties, account or site weighting, and moderator action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if you hit the 'best' hour, hidden/systemic factors can prevent front-page placement. Treat timing as a marginal factor and stay humble about deterministic claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose the right submission type (link, Show HN, Ask HN)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a normal submission for blog posts, research writeups, news articles, technical tutorials. Use Show HN when you made something people can try. Use Ask HN when you genuinely want answers or discussion, not as a disguised launch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show HN guidelines: it should be something you worked on personally, users should be able to try it, blog posts/newsletters/landing pages do not count, and you should be around to discuss it. Mislabeling post types (e.g., calling a homepage 'Show HN') often causes threads to go badly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow the Hacker News Guidelines (titles, source, promotion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Key rules in practice: submit the original source when possible; do not hype the title with ALL CAPS, exclamation points, or marketing language; do not change the title unless the original is misleading; do not use HN primarily for promotion; do not solicit upvotes, comments, or submissions; label video or PDF posts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HN rewards clear, plain, descriptive framing. 'Do not decorate it' — avoid clickbait or promotional language. Labeling formats ([video], [pdf]) is important and often overlooked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Etiquette and community behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Be kind, be curious, avoid snark, reply to the strongest version of what someone said, avoid shallow dismissals and flamewars, assume good faith, and follow the explicit prohibition on AI-generated or AI-edited comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you post your own work: be present, answer real questions, admit limitations, do not act like you are above criticism, and do not vanish after dropping the link. Social rules shape whether people give you the benefit of the doubt.

rubrics_metrics.name: What kinds of content usually do well
rubrics_metrics.description: Personal technical writing, useful tutorials, and thoughtful engineering blog posts tend to perform well; naked corporate promotion usually does not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Posts that teach something, explain a tradeoff clearly, share a real build story, or give technical readers concrete things to react to have a chance. If it reads like demand generation content, it probably will not perform well.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-post technical and editorial checklist
rubrics_metrics.description: Before posting: make sure the page loads fast; put the real subject in the title; remove hype, slogans, and vague claims; ensure the article is worth reading without a sales agenda; decide whether this should be a link post, Show HN, or Ask HN.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These practical checks address both the reader experience (fast loading, clear title) and community judgment (no hype, no sales agenda).

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-launch behavior checklist
rubrics_metrics.description: Right after posting: be around for the first hour; answer early questions clearly; fix obvious bugs or broken links fast; do not argue with every critic; do not ask friends to upvote.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early engagement and responsiveness help the thread; aggressive promotion or over-defensiveness harm reception.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to treat a post that 'dies'
rubrics_metrics.description: If it dies: do not panic, do not immediately repost, do not conclude the article was bad.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sometimes the window is short, timing was wrong, topic didn't match the day's audience, or randomness and hidden ranking factors intervened. Stay measured and learn rather than overreacting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use data tools sensibly (top-stories heatmap, analyses)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use analytics (e.g., a top-stories heatmap showing when high-scoring stories were created) as factual anchors, but understand their limitations: they show when top stories tend to appear, not your personal odds of success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many launch guides converge on similar windows; treat them as practical heuristics rather than revealed truth. Different analyses answer different questions (best chance per post vs. biggest total audience).

rubrics_metrics.name: The core conditions for posting success (the 'Real Answer')
rubrics_metrics.description: The best time to post is when these are all true: the relevant readers are awake; you can stick around to answer comments; the post is on-topic for HN; the title is plain and accurate; the thing you are sharing is genuinely interesting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If forced to pick a schedule use the default window (Tue-Thu, 14:00-17:00 UTC), experiment with Sunday night Pacific for low competition, and prefer Show HN for real products — but the deeper advice is: write something smart, say plainly what it is, follow the rules, and show up like a human.
